What is PowerShell and what makes it unique?

PowerShell is a cross-platform task automation shell and scripting language built on .NET. PowerShell 7+ is the current cross-platform version.

Key uniqueness: **Objects, not text** — unlike bash which passes text between commands, PowerShell passes .NET objects through the pipeline, enabling structured data manipulation.

```powershell
Write-Host "Hello, World!"
Write-Output "Hello, PowerShell!"  # goes to pipeline
"Hello from the pipeline"

# Run scripts
pwsh -File hello.ps1
pwsh -Command "Write-Host 'Hello'"

# Execution policy
Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser
```

How do variables, types, and strings work in PowerShell?

```powershell
# Variables start with $
$name = "Alice"
$age = 30
$flag = $true    # $true/$false/$null (not true/false/null)
$nothing = $null

# Type declarations
[int]$n = 42
[string]$s = "hello"
[datetime]$dt = Get-Date
[array]$arr = 1, 2, 3

# String interpolation (double quotes only)
$greeting = "Hello, $name!"
$greeting = "Age: $($age * 2)"   # expression in $()

# Verbatim string (single quotes — no interpolation)
$path = 'C:\Users\$name'   # $name is literal

# Here-string
$here = @"
Hello, $name!
Age: $age
"@

# String operations
$s = "Hello, World!"
$s.Length
$s.ToUpper()
$s.Substring(0, 5)  # "Hello"
$s.Contains("World")
$s.Replace("World","PS")
$s.Split(",")
$s.Trim()
$s -like "*World*"  # wildcard match
$s -match "W\w+"    # regex match → $Matches[0]
```

How do arrays and hashtables work in PowerShell?

```powershell
# Array
$arr = 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
$arr = @(1, 2, 3)
$arr[0]                # 1
$arr[-1]               # last element
$arr[1..3]             # slice: 2,3,4
$arr.Count
$arr -contains 3       # $true
$arr | Sort-Object
$arr | Sort-Object -Descending
$arr | Select-Object -First 3
$arr | Where-Object { $_ -gt 3 }  # filter

# Generic List (mutable, faster than array for add/remove)
$list = [System.Collections.Generic.List[string]]::new()
$list.Add("Alice")
$list.Contains("Alice")
$list.Remove("Alice")

# Hashtable (dictionary)
$h = @{ name = "Alice"; age = 30 }
$h["name"]          # "Alice"
$h.name             # dot notation
$h["city"] = "NYC"
$h.Remove("age")
$h.ContainsKey("name")
$h.Keys; $h.Values
$h.Count

# Ordered hashtable (maintains insertion order)
$oh = [ordered]@{ a = 1; b = 2; c = 3 }
```

How does the PowerShell pipeline and object manipulation work?

```powershell
# Everything is an object
$str = "Hello"
$str | Get-Member           # show all methods/properties
$str.GetType()

# Selecting, filtering, sorting
Get-Process | Select-Object Name, CPU, WorkingSet
Get-Process | Select-Object -First 5
Get-Process | Select-Object -ExpandProperty Name

Get-Process | Where-Object { $_.CPU -gt 100 }
Get-Process | Where-Object CPU -GT 100   # simplified syntax
Get-Service | Where-Object Status -EQ "Running"

Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending

# Grouping and measuring
Get-Process | Group-Object Company
Get-Process | Measure-Object CPU -Sum -Average -Maximum
Get-ChildItem | Measure-Object Length -Sum

# Formatting
Get-Process | Format-Table Name, CPU, Id -AutoSize
Get-Service | Format-List *

# Export
Get-Process | Export-Csv processes.csv -NoTypeInformation
Get-Process | ConvertTo-Json | Out-File processes.json
Import-Csv data.csv
```

How does file system manipulation and JSON work in PowerShell?

```powershell
# Navigation and listing
Get-Location
Set-Location C:\temp
Get-ChildItem                    # like ls
Get-ChildItem -Recurse -Filter "*.txt"

# File operations
New-Item -ItemType File "file.txt"
New-Item -ItemType Directory "mydir"
Copy-Item "src.txt" "dst.txt"
Move-Item "old.txt" "new.txt"
Remove-Item "file.txt"
Remove-Item "dir" -Recurse -Force
Test-Path "file.txt"   # $true or $false

# Read/Write
Get-Content "file.txt"                   # array of lines
Get-Content "file.txt" -Raw             # single string
Get-Content "file.txt" -Tail 10         # last 10 lines
Set-Content "file.txt" "Hello, World!"  # overwrite
Add-Content "file.txt" "New line"       # append

"line1","line2" | Out-File "file.txt"
Get-Content "file.txt" | Select-String "pattern"

# JSON
$json = Get-Content "data.json" -Raw | ConvertFrom-Json
$json.name
$obj | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 5 | Set-Content "out.json"

# CSV
Import-Csv "data.csv"
Export-Csv "out.csv" -NoTypeInformation

# Path operations
Split-Path "C:\temp\file.txt" -Leaf    # file.txt
Join-Path "C:\temp" "subdir" "file.txt"
```
